title: Fleet dotted-alias sweep for OPAG-276: does an ordinal-derived display reproduce frozen Backlog migration aliases
description: opum-agent (OPAG-276) asked whether a Quest-native, immutable, append-only dotted DISPLAY for child tasks (the operator's preferred fifth option from the canonical-id ADR review, QCLI-250) would collide with the dotted aliases Backlog migration already froze onto tasks fleet-wide. This task records the direct measurement, not a relay of it -- per this fleet's own rule that a filing record citing a measurement it did not itself perform is indistinguishable from the measurement to a later reader. opum-agent will cite this task id from OPAG-276 rather than restating the numbers.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Full enumeration of every dotted Backlog-migration alias across the fleet (all 7 migrated repos: quest-cli, opum-agent, opum-doc, lore-cli, opum-cli-e2e, lore-web, quest-web), at every nesting depth, checked against each records real parentId siblings -- recorded in full, not sampled
Every mismatch between the naive ordinal-derived position and the frozen alias is root-caused against the source migration receipt, ruling in or out a migration bug
The ordinal-tie tiebreak finding is recorded with both the wrong answer (the tiebreak that was tried first and silently broke a real tie) and the right one, not just the right one
The multi-level dotted-alias decomposition (e.g. PREFIX-N.M.K) is documented with a concrete verified example showing each dot segment is an independent real parentId edge

plan: 1. Shallow-clone all 9 sibling fleet repos read-only into scratchpad, plus use quest-cli own checkout, without touching any sibling working tree
2. Enumerate every task/completed record parentId, ordinal, createdAt, aliases across all 10 repos
3. Extract dotted-alias hits (any nesting depth), group by each records REAL parentId, sort siblings by ordinal then createdAt then id as tiebreaks
4. Compare naive position to the aliass local (last) dot segment; catch and fix a tiebreak bug found in the first pass
5. Root-cause every mismatch against the source migration receipt mappings
6. Verify multi-level dotted aliases decompose into independent real parentId edges
implementationNotes: Methodology: read-only shallow clones (git clone --depth 1 --branch dev) of all 9 sibling fleet repos into this session own scratchpad directory, never touching any sibling sessions actual working tree (per fleet norm: verify a sibling through refs/export to own scratch space, not by operating on its checkout). Combined with this repos own live checkout. Population: 7 of 10 fleet repos have a .quest/migrations/backlog/ receipt and nonzero dotted aliases (quest-cli, opum-agent, opum-doc, lore-cli, opum-cli-e2e, lore-web, quest-web); opum-cli-e2e migrated but produced zero dotted aliases (flat source, no subtasks). 3 repos are native Quest with no migration and zero dotted aliases (opum-web, opum-marketplace, opum-fleet) -- out of scope by construction. Enumerated every task/completed record parentId, ordinal, createdAt, aliases fleet-wide; extracted every dotted alias at any nesting depth; grouped by each records REAL parentId (Quest own graph field, not inferred from the alias string); sorted siblings by ordinal ascending, then createdAt ascending, then id as tiebreaks; compared the resulting 1-based naive position to the aliass LOCAL (last) dot segment.

Result: 206 dotted-alias positions checked fleet-wide. 201 (97.6%) exactly reproduced by the naive ordinal-then-createdAt-then-id position count. 5 did not -- all 5 in opum-doc, zero unexplained. Direct answer to the yes/no this was measuring: NO, the frozen set is not always reproducible from ordinal -- there is at least one repo where the two producers (frozen migration alias vs computed dotted display) can and do disagree, not merely could in theory.

The 5 mismatches, root-caused (AC2): all downstream of exactly 2 numbering gaps in opum-doc. ODOC-63: children .1-.7 exist, then jumps to .23/.24 -- 15 missing numbers (.8-.22). ODOC-71: .1-.5 exist, .6 is missing, then .7-.9 exist -- 1 missing number. Checked against opum-doc own migration receipt (.quest/migrations/backlog/*.json, 133 source-to-target mappings): none of the missing numbers (ODOC-63.8 through .22, ODOC-71.6) appear anywhere in the mappings array -- not migrated, not logged as excluded (the receipt schema has no excluded/skipped field at all), simply absent from the source scan entirely. Conclusion: this rules OUT a migration bug. Backlog own source numbering already had these gaps before migration ran -- almost certainly subtasks deleted in Backlog pre-migration, consistent with Backlogs dot-suffixed counters not being reclaimed on delete (the same non-global-counter defect the canonical-id ADR cites). Every parent WITHOUT a gap reproduces perfectly; the two parents downstream of a gap are exactly where a naive count-of-children allocator diverges from the frozen alias. This is a concrete, proven instance of gap-below-a-taken-number-is-not-free, not a hypothetical: an allocator for a Quest-native dotted display MUST enumerate the occupied dotted set per parent (a cheap one-time scan), not assume density from child count.

Tiebreak finding (AC3), recorded with the wrong answer alongside the right one, as requested -- a future implementer who reaches for the wrong one should find this first. quest-cli own QCLI-2 has two children sharing an IDENTICAL ordinal value (12000): QCLI-176 (created 2026-08-04) and QCLI-188 (created 2026-08-01, i.e. earlier), with frozen aliases QCLI-2.10 and QCLI-2.9 respectively. WRONG (first pass, tried and caught): breaking the tie by file-enumeration/directory-read order (or equivalently, id-numeric order: 176 sorts before 188) gives QCLI-176 position 9 and QCLI-188 position 10 -- exactly backwards from the frozen aliases (176 should be .10, 188 should be .9). This is not a contrived failure: id-numeric order is the tiebreak someone would reach for first, since it looks like the obvious deterministic fallback. RIGHT: breaking the tie by createdAt ascending reproduces the frozen aliases exactly -- QCLI-188 (earlier createdAt) gets position 9 (matches .9), QCLI-176 (later createdAt) gets position 10 (matches .10). Generalized rule verified fleet-wide: sort siblings by ordinal ascending, then createdAt ascending, then id as a final tiebreak only for genuine simultaneous-timestamp ties -- this reproduced all 201 non-gap-affected cases exactly, including every tie encountered. Tiebreak choice is a load-bearing design decision for any ordinal-derived dotted allocator, not an implementation detail: the wrong choice silently breaks a real case that the right choice solves cleanly, with no error or signal that anything went wrong.

Multi-level dotted-alias decomposition (AC4), verified concretely, retiring the "what does PREFIX-N.M.K mean" question. quest-cli record QCLI-191 carries alias QCLI-97.10.1 and has parentId QCLI-190 (verified via quest task view QCLI-191 --json and reading .quest/tasks/QCLI-191.json directly). QCLI-190 itself carries the alias QCLI-97.10 and (by the same pattern) its own parentId pointing at QCLI-97. So a two-segment dotted alias is not a single flat lookup or a new kind of hierarchy -- it decomposes into two independently-correct single-level derivations composed: QCLI-190 is child #10 of QCLI-97 (frozen alias .10), and QCLI-191 is child #1 of QCLI-190 (frozen alias .10.1, local suffix 1). Verified fleet-wide: every multi-level dotted alias found (12 in quest-cli under QCLI-97, 17 in opum-doc under ODOC-55/ODOC-63, 11 in lore-cli under LCLI-283) decomposes the same way and is included in the 201/206 perfect-match count using the SAME algorithm (group by real parentId, compare to the aliass LOCAL/last dot segment) with no special-casing for depth. A prospective two-level case such as opum-agent OPAG-274 to parent OPAG-273 to parent OPAG-245 would compose the same way, PROVIDED both levels have ordinals -- which is a separate, still-open question (opum-agent own concern: 25 of 36 parented records there carry no ordinal at all) that this historical sweep cannot resolve either way, since there is no frozen alias to check a fully-new hierarchy against.

Answer: NO, ordinal does not always reproduce the frozen alias -- 201 of 206 fleet-wide dotted-alias positions match a naive ordinal-then-createdAt-then-id derivation, 5 do not, all 5 in opum-doc and fully root-caused to 2 genuine numbering gaps already present in Backlog own source data before migration ran (verified against opum-doc migration receipt: the missing numbers never appear in its 133 mappings, ruling out a migration bug). Also recorded: a tiebreak-choice finding (createdAt ascending reproduces a real ordinal tie exactly; id-numeric/file order silently gets it backwards) and verified that multi-level dotted aliases decompose into independent real parentId edges, retiring the "what does X.Y.Z mean" question. Method: read-only shallow clones of all 9 sibling repos into this session own scratchpad (never touched a sibling working tree) plus this repo own live checkout; full enumeration, not sampling. Reported to opum-agent in-session; this task is the citable record per the fleet rule that a filing record must be defensible by whoever performed the measurement.
